Jordan: Customer (acct: acme-analytics) hit prolonged 429s + p95 latency spikes during a midday burst. They say autoscale started but requests queued for >30s. Can we triage?
Katie: Which deployment mode? Dedicated? Any model details?
Jordan: Dedicated / region us-west2 / model rwl-13b-q4_0 / min_replicas=2 max_replicas=20. Customer reports a scale event at 12:02 where desired jumped to 12 but only 4 warm replicas ended up serving. Queue/backpressure visible.
Leo: :eyes: Can you paste the autoscaler and provisioner events? Also any preflight/errors from the node pool side.
Jordan: Pasted snippets below (redacted):
```
autoscaler: eval -> desired_replicas=12 current=4 reason=provision_throttle
provisioner: 2026-09-14T12:02:05Z WARN preflight quota_check=rate_limit status=429
provisioner: 2026-09-14T12:02:09Z INFO spawn worker id=wp-89 init=start
provisioner: 2026-09-14T12:02:15Z ERROR failed_create instance_quota_exceeded
worker-init: model_load_time=18s kvcache_restore=4s
```
Katie: That looks like two separate problems: (1) preflight/API rate limit returning 429s preventing new instance creation, (2) long model init time (18s) limiting how quickly warm replicas become ready. Together they explain the gap.
Tara: Customer says they have bursty traffic (ad-hoc analytics queries) so warm pool would help. Do they have warm_pool configured?
Jordan: They do not have a reserved warm_pool. Their autoscaler is default (no warm pool). They expected Dedicated to fast scale.
Leo: We should confirm if the account hit cloud provider quota or our internal request rate limiter. Check quota history for the customer's org at 12:00-12:05. Also look at the provisioner logs for 429 retries/backoff.
Katie: Quick repro steps I ran in staging: send steady ramp from 50->700 concurrent requests over 60s against a small dedicated tenant. Observed similar pattern: desired climbs, provision attempts get throttled by provider API, backoff kicks in, only ~30% of desired become ready within 60s.
SRE-Bot: alert: provisioner_rate_limit_exceeded for org=acme-analytics count=27 window=1m
Jordan: Customer impact: timeouts in their app, some requests retried and charged for extra tokens. They're asking for short-term mitigation and long-term fix.
Tara: Short term: advise customer to enable warm_pool with min 4 prewarmed nodes and lower model load latency via quantized variant if possible. Also suggest temporary increase in min_replicas to 4 to avoid cold gap.
Leo: Ops-side mitigation: request rate limit increase from cloud provider for that org or batch creation calls to avoid hitting provider rate limits. For immediate relief we can pin more capacity for them (provision a few reserved instances in their Dedicated pool) — needs billing/CS approval.
Katie: Long term: two engineering actions: (A) make provisioner respect provider rate-limits more gracefully with concurrency windowing + async enqueue so desired != in-flight_creates; (B) add an optional warm_pool feature in Dedicated controlplane UI with prewarm autoscaling advice and suggested warm size based on historical burst patterns.
Jordan: I've emailed CS and assigned a ticket to Billing for a short-term reserved capacity quote. CS will ask customer to test with warm_pool + min_replicas=4.
Leo: I'll create an ENG-PLATFORM backlog ticket for provider-rate-limit handling (assign to @Leo). Katie, can you take the warm_pool design doc?
Katie: Yep, will draft and include heuristics: recommend warm_pool = max(ceil(peak_qps / model_throughput), 2) and prewarm model variants.
SRE-Bot: note: follow-up commands for triage: `kubectl logs -n provisioner deploy/provisioner | grep 1978001111` and `curl -s https://metrics.internal/api?q=provisioner:rate_limit&period=5m&org=acme-analytics`
Jordan: I'll run those and DM the snippets. For now customer is testing increasing min_replicas and enabling warm_pool. Next update in 30m. :thumbsup:
